sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Rockingham County?
sections.html:
The Tax Administration office handles both sides of the bill. In Rockingham County the jobs of assessor and collector are combined under one Tax Administrator, with an assessment division and a collection division. The office sits in the Rockingham County Governmental Center at 371 NC Hwy 65 in Reidsville, and it keeps Monday through Friday hours from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The listed phone is 336-342-8305, and mail goes to PO Box 68, Wentworth, NC 27375.

The assessment division lists, appraises and assesses real property, business personal property and individual personal property, and it also handles ownership transfers and record maintenance. The collection division bills and collects current and delinquent taxes for the county, the City of Eden, the City of Reidsville, the Town of Madison, the Town of Mayodan, the Town of Stoneville and 18 rural fire districts. If you own a house in one of those towns, you will usually see several levies on one bill.

Sellers in Rockingham County should know the scale of the roll. The county describes itself as having about 55,800 real estate parcels, 4,000 businesses, 98,800 registered motor vehicles and 4,350 personal property manufactured homes. Rates are set by the Board of County Commissioners, each fire district and each city or town council, and the county says they are established in June with bills mailed in late July.

sections.h2: When are Rockingham County property taxes due, and what happens if I pay late?
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1, and taxes paid before January 6 carry no interest. The county's own page said that the 2025 bills could be paid without interest until January 5, 2026, which tracks the statewide rule that interest begins on January 6.

After that, state law adds two percent interest from January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or fraction after that. Rockingham County offers several ways to pay a bill:

  • Online by credit or debit card through the county's payment-service link, or by e-check through a second link
  • By phone at 1-866-251-3264, with your bill in hand
  • By mail to Rockingham County Tax Collector, PO Box 68, Wentworth, NC 27375-0068
  • In person at the Governmental Center in Reidsville

A mailed payment counts as received on the postmark date. A county or town may also adopt a prepayment discount schedule, so ask the collector whether one applies to the bill you hold.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Rockingham County property value?
sections.html:
You have four steps, and the first two cost nothing. Rockingham County's appeal page describes an informal review, then the Board of Equalization and Review, then the state Property Tax Commission, then the North Carolina Court of Appeals.

The informal step starts when you call the Real Property Division and speak with an appraiser, who will recheck the record and the value. The county says informal appeals may be filed from January 1 until the Board adjourns. The Board of Equalization and Review is appointed by the county commissioners, is separate from the tax office staff, and hears appeals beginning in April of each year.

Rockingham County appeal steps as printed on the county appeal page
StepBodyWhat the county page says
1Real Property DivisionInformal review with an appraiser, open from January 1 until the Board adjourns
2Board of Equalization and ReviewAppointed by the commissioners, hears appeals starting in April
3NC Property Tax CommissionFive members, meets in Raleigh, appeals heard by application and appointment
4NC Court of AppealsFor owners dissatisfied after all other steps

Statewide, the written request to the county board must come before the board adjourns, and an appeal to the Commission is filed within 30 days after the board mails its decision. Between reappraisals the county notes that value changes are limited by G.S. 105-287.

sections.h2: How often does Rockingham County reappraise real estate?
sections.html:
At least once every eight years under state law, and counties may choose a shorter cycle. Rockingham County completed a reappraisal that took effect with the 2024 tax year, and its tax office published a revaluation FAQ and an appeal process page for that cycle. Ask the Tax Administration office for the date of the next scheduled reappraisal, because the county sets it by resolution.

A reappraisal resets every parcel to market value as of its effective date. It does not set the tax rate, which the commissioners and each town adopt separately. Owners who sell soon after a reappraisal should compare the new assessed value with the contract price, since the two numbers are not tied to each other.

sections.h2: Are there tax breaks for Rockingham County homeowners?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three relief programs, and an owner may use only one of them. The county posts the 2026 Application for Property Tax Relief on its Tax Forms page, and the state form is AV-9 filed with the county assessor, not the Department of Revenue.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or half the appraised value of the permanent residence, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled whose income is within the limit. The 2026 income limit printed on the state form is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4.0% of income at or under the limit and 5.0% of income above it up to 150% of the limit, which the 2026 state form prints as $58,200. Excess tax is deferred and becomes a lien.

The deferral matters in a sale. Under the circuit breaker, deferred taxes for the preceding three years become due when the owner transfers the property or stops living in it as a permanent residence. A new application is needed every year, and the state says to file during the listing period, which runs through January 31, with the assessor accepting applications through June 1.

sections.h2: What does a Rockingham County seller owe in property tax at closing?
sections.html:
The seller owes the share of the year's bill for the months of ownership, and any unpaid prior-year taxes. A tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date each year, with penalties, interest and costs attaching at the same time, so a delinquent balance must be cleared for a buyer to get clean title.

If a bill goes unpaid, the county can bring a foreclosure action much like a mortgage foreclosure, serving the record owner and other lienholders. The sale is a public auction at the courthouse door, and the person redeeming before confirmation pays all taxes plus penalties, interest and costs. A bidder may deposit up to 20% of the bid, and the commissioner's fee can reach five percent of the price.

Before you list a Rockingham County house, ask the collection division for a payoff figure on every parcel number, including any fire district charge. Then ask your closing attorney to prorate the current year. For a cash sale of a house with back taxes, the buyer's attorney will want the balance paid from proceeds at the table.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Rockingham County property taxes?
faqs.a: You pay the Rockingham County Tax Collector, online, by phone at 1-866-251-3264, by mail to PO Box 68 in Wentworth, or at the Governmental Center in Reidsville. Keep your bill handy, since the phone option requires it.

faqs.q: Is the Tax Assessor a different office from the Tax Collector in Rockingham County?
faqs.a: No. Rockingham County combines the assessor and collector roles under one Tax Administrator, with an assessment division and a collection division inside the same office.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my value by phone?
faqs.a: Yes for the informal step. You can call the Real Property Division and speak with an appraiser, who will review the record and value. The formal step before the Board of Equalization and Review must be requested in writing on the county form.

faqs.q: What if I sell my Rockingham County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: The lien follows the parcel, so the balance must be paid for title to pass cleanly. Your closing attorney normally pays it from your sale proceeds, so request a payoff amount from the collection division before closing.

faqs.q: Which towns send a tax bill collected by the county?
faqs.a: Besides the county bill, the collection division collects for the City of Eden, the City of Reidsville, the Town of Madison, the Town of Mayodan, the Town of Stoneville and 18 rural fire districts, so one parcel can carry several levies.
